heard: We shortened an asteroid's orbit 32 minutes just by crashing into it. In September 2022, NASA slammed a box-shaped spacecraft into dimorphos, a moonlit 7 million miles from Earth. The DART mission targeted this 530-foot wide rock at a staggering speed of 14,000 miles per hour. While telescopes like James Webb watched, an Italian CubeSat caught the moment the probe hit the surface. Mission controllers only expected the violent collision to nudge the asteroid orbit by about 73 seconds. But the impact blasted so much debris into space that the recoil acted like a massive rocket engine. This amplified the push so much that the nearly 12-hour orbit changed by over half an hour. This is how we learned to steer a giant space rock by crashing into it. You
